classification.difficultyReason: Identify the exterior boundary, combine two semicircular arcs, and use matching ticks to count four equal shoulders and two equal ends.

content.prompt: Find the approximate value of the perimeter of the figure to the right, using $\pi\approx3.14$.

spec.description: Horizontal rectangle with an upper and lower semicircle sharing vertically aligned diameter endpoints. Both internal diameters are dashed red, labelled 3.2 m, and have red centre points. Four exposed horizontal shoulders have single matching ticks; the upper-right shoulder is labelled 2 m. Both vertical ends have double matching ticks; the right end is labelled 1.5 m. Ordinary source blue lines become black, and semantic red becomes house red. No region is shaded.
spec.mathematics: Two semicircles of diameter 3.2 m contribute one complete circumference. Four equal horizontal boundary segments are each 2 m; two equal vertical boundary segments are each 1.5 m. Internal diameters are excluded from the perimeter.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, equality marks and internal diameter guides are visible.

answer.short:
$21.048\ \mathrm{m}$

The two semicircular arcs make one circumference; add the six exposed straight edges.
answer.worked:
The two semicircular arcs together have the circumference of a circle of diameter $3.2\ \mathrm{m}$. The dashed diameters are internal.

$$\begin{align*}P&=\pi\times3.2+4\times2+2\times1.5\\P&=3.2\pi+11\ \mathrm{m}\\P&\approx3.2\times3.14+11\ \mathrm{m}\\P&\approx21.048\ \mathrm{m}\end{align*}$$
